rows.en: The mental health and psychosocial well-being of people residing in camps and camp-like settings is significantly impacted by the extent to which they can participate in decision-making that affects their lives, access information, and access appropriate facilities and services. The distress caused by their displacement can be exacerbated or mitigated depending on the degree to which their sense of agency and independence is promoted or diminished.
rows.ne: शिविर तथा शिविरजस्ता परिवेशमा बसोबास गर्ने व्यक्तिहरू आफ्नो जीवनलाई असर गर्ने निर्णय प्रक्रियामा कति सहभागी हुन सक्छन्, सूचना कति प्राप्त गर्न सक्छन् र उपयुक्त सुविधा तथा सेवामा कति पहुँच राख्छन् भन्ने कुराले उनीहरूको मानसिक स्वास्थ्य तथा मनोसामाजिक कल्याणमा उल्लेखनीय प्रभाव पार्छ। उनीहरूमा आफ्नो तर्फबाट निर्णय र कार्य गर्न सक्ने क्षमता तथा स्वतन्त्रताको अनुभूति कति बढाइन्छ वा घटाइन्छ भन्ने आधारमा विस्थापनका कारण उत्पन्न कष्ट बढ्न वा कम हुन सक्छ।
rows.bt: The extent to which people living in camps and camp-like settings can participate in decision-making processes that affect their lives, can obtain information and have access to appropriate facilities and services has a significant effect on their mental health and psychosocial well-being. Distress arising from displacement can increase or decrease depending on how much their sense of ability and freedom to make decisions and act on their own behalf is increased or decreased.
rows.note: Mental health and psychosocial well-being reuse supplied unreviewed candidates. Distress is rendered as ordinary displacement-related hardship, not as a diagnostic term. Agency retains the sense of being able to decide and act for oneself. The draft renders independence as self-reliance, which can imply supporting oneself rather than freedom from others' control. The revision preserves the source's sense of independence alongside agency.

rows.en: CCCM actors, through their direct and regular interaction with displaced families and communities, have a key role to play in enhancing the well-being of those living in displacement sites (see also Minimum Standards for Camp Management; MSCM).
rows.ne: विस्थापित परिवार र समुदायसँग हुने प्रत्यक्ष तथा नियमित अन्तरक्रियामार्फत विस्थापित व्यक्तिहरू बसोबास गर्ने स्थलमा रहेका व्यक्तिहरूको कल्याण बढाउन CCCM सम्बद्ध पक्षको महत्त्वपूर्ण भूमिका छ (शिविर व्यवस्थापनका न्यूनतम मापदण्डहरू; MSCM पनि हेर्नुहोस्)।
rows.bt: Through direct and regular interaction with displaced families and communities, CCCM stakeholders have an important role in increasing the well-being of people at sites where displaced people live (see also the Minimum Standards for Camp Management; MSCM).
rows.note: Proposed glossary additions: well-being = [Nepali wording recorded in terminology evidence]; Minimum Standards for Camp Management = [Nepali wording recorded in terminology evidence] [Nepali wording recorded in terminology evidence] [Nepali wording recorded in terminology evidence] [Nepali wording recorded in terminology evidence]. MSCM is retained. The source identifies a key role CCCM actors have to play; the draft asserts that they already perform that role. The revision states their role without asserting its actual performance.

rows.en: CCCM actors can integrate MHPSS into programming by (see MSP activity 1.1 and MSCM 4.1) to:
rows.ne: CCCM सम्बद्ध पक्षले कार्यक्रम तर्जुमा तथा कार्यान्वयनमा MHPSS एकीकृत गर्न निम्न माध्यमहरू अपनाउन सक्छन् (MSP गतिविधि 1.1 र MSCM 4.1 हेर्नुहोस्)।
rows.bt: Parties associated with CCCM can adopt the following means to integrate MHPSS into programme planning and implementation (see MSP activity 1.1 and MSCM 4.1).
rows.note: The source phrase 'by (see MSP activity 1.1 and MSCM 4.1) to:' has an unresolved grammatical connection; the draft uses a means-based introduction without assigning a purpose to the dangling 'to'.

rows.en: ▶ Including MHPSS in multi-sectoral site needs assessments (see MSP activity 1.2 and MSCM 4.2).
rows.ne: ▶ स्थलका बहुक्षेत्रीय आवश्यकताको लेखाजोखामा MHPSS समावेश गर्ने (MSP गतिविधि 1.2 र MSCM 4.2 हेर्नुहोस्)।
rows.bt: ▶ Include MHPSS in assessments of the site's multisectoral needs (see MSP Activity 1.2 and MSCM 4.2).

rows.en: ▶ Engaging in monitoring and advocacy regarding gaps in services and needs, through close collaboration and exchange between CCCM and MHPSS actors (see MSP activity 3.1 and MSCM 4.1, 4.2).
rows.ne: ▶ CCCM र MHPSS सम्बद्ध पक्षहरूबीच निकट सहकार्य तथा आदानप्रदानमार्फत सेवामा रहेका कमी र आवश्यकताका सम्बन्धमा अनुगमन तथा पैरवी गर्ने (MSP गतिविधि 3.1 र MSCM 4.1, 4.2 हेर्नुहोस्)।
rows.bt: ▶ Monitor and advocate regarding gaps and needs in services through close collaboration and exchange between CCCM and MHPSS actors (see MSP Activity 3.1 and MSCM 4.1, 4.2).

rows.en: ▶ Providing humanitarian assistance in ways that support mental health and psychosocial well-being (see MSP activity 3.1), by:
rows.ne: ▶ निम्न तरिकाले मानसिक स्वास्थ्य तथा मनोसामाजिक कल्याणलाई सहयोग पुग्ने गरी मानवीय सहायता प्रदान गर्ने (MSP गतिविधि 3.1 हेर्नुहोस्)।
rows.bt: ▶ Provide humanitarian assistance in ways that support mental health and psychosocial well-being, as follows (see MSP Activity 3.1).
rows.note: Mental health and psychosocial well-being reuse supplied unreviewed candidates.

rows.en: • Engaging site residents in decision-making related to the management of the site (e.g. by supporting inclusive and representative governance structures, child committees, sectoral committees and community-led initiatives; see MSCM 2.1, 2.4), especially related to sites for planned MHPSS activities (e.g. MSP activities 3.4, 3.6, 3.9).
rows.ne: • स्थलको व्यवस्थापनसम्बन्धी निर्णय प्रक्रियामा स्थलका बासिन्दालाई सहभागी गराउने (उदाहरणका लागि, समावेशी र प्रतिनिधिमूलक शासन संरचना, बाल समिति, क्षेत्रगत समिति र समुदायको नेतृत्वमा सञ्चालित पहललाई सहयोग गरेर; MSCM 2.1, 2.4 हेर्नुहोस्), विशेष गरी योजनाबद्ध MHPSS गतिविधिहरू सञ्चालन गरिने स्थलसम्बन्धी निर्णयमा (उदाहरणका लागि, MSP गतिविधिहरू 3.4, 3.6, 3.9)।
rows.bt: • Involve site residents in decision-making processes concerning site management (for example, by supporting inclusive and representative governance structures, children's committees, sectoral committees and community-led initiatives; see MSCM 2.1, 2.4), particularly in decisions concerning sites where planned MHPSS activities will be carried out (for example, MSP Activities 3.4, 3.6, 3.9).

rows.en: • Ensuring appropriate and inclusive planning to promote adequate protection and assistance, according to site residents’ needs (including mental health related needs), throughout the lifecycle of the site (see MSP activity 2.1, MSCM 1.2, 5).
rows.ne: • स्थलको सम्पूर्ण जीवनचक्रभरि स्थलका बासिन्दाका आवश्यकता (मानसिक स्वास्थ्यसम्बन्धी आवश्यकतासहित) अनुसार पर्याप्त संरक्षण तथा सहायता प्रवर्द्धन गर्न उपयुक्त र समावेशी योजना सुनिश्चित गर्ने (MSP गतिविधि 2.1, MSCM 1.2, 5 हेर्नुहोस्)।
rows.bt: • Ensure appropriate and inclusive planning to promote adequate protection and assistance according to site residents' needs (including mental health needs) throughout the site's entire life cycle (see MSP Activity 2.1, MSCM 1.2, 5).
rows.note: General protection and assistance planning guidance; review pending. Mental health reuses the supplied unreviewed candidate.

rows.en: • Providing sufficient communal space e.g. for socio-relational and recreational activities (e.g. for MSP activities 3.4, 3.6, 3.9, also see MSCM 3.1, 3.2).
rows.ne: • पर्याप्त सामुदायिक स्थान उपलब्ध गराउने, उदाहरणका लागि सामाजिक सम्बन्धसम्बन्धी तथा मनोरञ्जनात्मक गतिविधिका लागि (उदाहरणका लागि, MSP गतिविधिहरू 3.4, 3.6, 3.9 का लागि; MSCM 3.1, 3.2 पनि हेर्नुहोस्)।
rows.bt: • Provide sufficient community space, for example for activities related to social connections and recreation (for example, for MSP activities 3.4, 3.6, 3.9; see also MSCM 3.1, 3.2).
rows.note: The draft narrows socio-relational activities to activities that increase social connections. The revision retains the broader relationship-related meaning without requiring an increase.

rows.en: • Ensuring that site residents live in a dignified environment that promotes mental health and psychosocial well-being and is safe, secure, and physically, socially and culturally appropriate (see MSP activity 3.1, MSCM 3.1, 3.2).
rows.ne: • स्थलका बासिन्दा मानसिक स्वास्थ्य र मनोसामाजिक कल्याण प्रवर्द्धन गर्ने, सुरक्षित र सुरक्षाको प्रत्याभूति भएको तथा भौतिक, सामाजिक र सांस्कृतिक रूपमा उपयुक्त मर्यादित वातावरणमा बस्ने सुनिश्चित गर्ने (MSP गतिविधि 3.1, MSCM 3.1, 3.2 हेर्नुहोस्)।
rows.bt: • Ensure that site residents live in a dignified environment that promotes mental health and psychosocial well-being, is safe and assured of security, and is physically, socially and culturally appropriate (see MSP Activity 3.1, MSCM 3.1, 3.2).
rows.note: Mental health and psychosocial well-being wording reuses the supplied unreviewed candidates T157 and T005.

rows.en: • Organizing community discussions and accessible feedback and complaints mechanisms that are responsive and contribute to improving accountability towards the affected populations (see MSP activity 2.1, MSCM 2.3).
rows.ne: • समुदायमा छलफल आयोजना गर्ने तथा प्रतिक्रिया र गुनासोप्रति उत्तरदायी भई प्रभावित जनसमुदायप्रतिको जवाफदेहिता सुधार्न योगदान गर्ने पहुँचयोग्य प्रतिक्रिया तथा गुनासो संयन्त्रहरूको व्यवस्था गर्ने (MSP गतिविधि 2.1, MSCM 2.3 हेर्नुहोस्)।
rows.bt: • Organize community discussions and establish accessible feedback and complaint mechanisms that contribute to improving accountability to the affected population by being responsive to feedback and complaints (see MSP Activity 2.1, MSCM 2.3).

rows.en: ▶ Organizing orientations in basic psychosocial support (e.g. psychological first aid) for site management teams, including the identification and referral of children and adults who may need MHPSS services and supports (see MSP activity 3.2 and MSCM 4.3).
rows.ne: ▶ MHPSS सेवा र सहयोग आवश्यक पर्न सक्ने बालबालिका तथा वयस्कको पहिचान गर्ने र सम्बन्धित सेवामा पठाउने कार्यसमेत समेटेर स्थल व्यवस्थापन टोलीहरूका लागि आधारभूत मनोसामाजिक सहयोग (जस्तै, [psychological first aid]) सम्बन्धी अभिमुखीकरण आयोजना गर्ने (MSP गतिविधि 3.2 र MSCM 4.3 हेर्नुहोस्)।
rows.bt: ▶ Organize orientation on basic psychosocial support (for example, [psychological first aid]) for site management teams, including identifying children and adults who may need MHPSS services and support and referring them to relevant services (see MSP activity 3.2 and MSCM 4.3).
rows.note: The named intervention is retained exactly in English, while the orientation, identification and referral guidance is drafted in Nepali.

rows.en: ▶ Referring people to MHPSS activities, including to mental health care providers, as needed.
rows.ne: ▶ आवश्यकताअनुसार मानिसहरूलाई MHPSS गतिविधिहरूका लागि सम्बन्धित सेवामा पठाउने कार्य गर्ने, जसमा मानसिक स्वास्थ्य सेवा प्रदायकहरूकहाँ पठाउने कार्य पनि समावेश हुन्छ।
rows.bt: ▶ Refer people to relevant services for MHPSS activities as needed, including referrals to mental health service providers.
rows.note: Mental health care wording reuses [Nepali wording recorded in terminology evidence] [Nepali wording recorded in terminology evidence] [Nepali wording recorded in terminology evidence] from the supplied unreviewed activity 3.10 candidate; no clinical validation is claimed.

rows.en: ▶ Including key messages on mental health and psychosocial support (see MSP activity 3.3) as part of regular provision of information to site residents utilizing their preferred communication formats and languages, including on services available in the site (MSCM 2.2).
rows.ne: ▶ स्थलका बासिन्दालाई उनीहरूले रुचाएका सञ्चारका स्वरूप र भाषाहरू प्रयोग गरी नियमित रूपमा सूचना प्रदान गर्दा स्थलमा उपलब्ध सेवासम्बन्धी जानकारीसमेत समेट्ने र मानसिक स्वास्थ्य तथा मनोसामाजिक सहयोगसम्बन्धी मुख्य सन्देशहरू पनि समावेश गर्ने (MSP गतिविधि 3.3 हेर्नुहोस्; MSCM 2.2)।
rows.bt: ▶ When regularly providing information to site residents using their preferred forms of communication and languages, also cover information about services available at the site and include key messages on mental health and psychosocial support (see MSP Activity 3.3; MSCM 2.2).
rows.note: The composite MHPSS wording reuses the supplied unreviewed candidate T001.

rows.en: ▶ Monitoring MHPSS-related outputs and outcomes (e.g. improvements in well-being following a participatory approach to the management of the site).
rows.ne: ▶ MHPSS सम्बन्धी प्रतिफलहरू र परिणामहरूको अनुगमन गर्ने (जस्तै, स्थलको व्यवस्थापनमा सहभागितामूलक पद्धति अपनाएपछि कल्याणमा भएको सुधार)।
rows.bt: ▶ Monitor MHPSS-related outputs and outcomes (e.g., improvement in well-being after adopting a participatory approach to site management).
rows.note: Proposed missing recurring terms: monitoring = [Nepali wording recorded in terminology evidence]; outputs = [Nepali wording recorded in terminology evidence]; outcomes = [Nepali wording recorded in terminology evidence]. These are drafting proposals, not glossary amendments.

rows.en: Key consideration 9: Integrating MHPSS into shelter and settlement programming
rows.ne: मुख्य विचारणीय पक्ष 9: आश्रय तथा बसोबाससम्बन्धी कार्यक्रम तर्जुमा तथा सञ्चालनमा MHPSS एकीकृत गर्ने
rows.bt: Key consideration 9: Integrating MHPSS into the design and implementation of shelter and settlement programmes
rows.note: Proposed missing recurring terms: shelter = [Nepali wording recorded in terminology evidence]; settlement = [Nepali wording recorded in terminology evidence]; programming = [Nepali wording recorded in terminology evidence] [Nepali wording recorded in terminology evidence] [Nepali wording recorded in terminology evidence] [Nepali wording recorded in terminology evidence].

rows.en: Living conditions during humanitarian crises can affect people’s physical and mental well-being as much as the initial crisis or disaster. Overcrowding, poor ventilation, inadequate or unsafe toilets and washing facilities, inadequate menstrual hygiene facilities, inadequate water supply and poor waste management all increase stress, protection risks and ill health.
rows.ne: मानवीय सङ्कटहरूका बेला जीवनयापनका अवस्थाले मानिसहरूको शारीरिक तथा मानसिक कल्याणमा प्रारम्भिक सङ्कट वा विपद्ले जत्तिकै असर पार्न सक्छन्। अत्यधिक भीडभाड, हावाको कमजोर आवागमन, अपर्याप्त वा असुरक्षित शौचालय र धुनेपखाल्ने सुविधा, महिनावारीको स्वच्छताका लागि अपर्याप्त सुविधा, अपर्याप्त पानी आपूर्ति र फोहोरको कमजोर व्यवस्थापन सबैले तनाव, संरक्षणसम्बन्धी जोखिम र अस्वस्थता बढाउँछन्।
rows.bt: During humanitarian crises, living conditions can affect people's physical and mental well-being as much as the initial crisis or disaster. Excessive overcrowding, poor ventilation, inadequate or unsafe toilets and washing facilities, inadequate facilities for menstrual hygiene, inadequate water supply and poor waste management all increase stress, protection-related risks and ill health.
rows.note: Physical and mental well-being remain distinct from psychosocial well-being, and all listed living-condition risks are retained.

rows.en: Shelter actors can integrate MHPSS into programming by:
rows.ne: आश्रयसम्बन्धी सम्बद्ध पक्षहरूले निम्न उपायबाट कार्यक्रम तर्जुमा तथा सञ्चालनमा MHPSS एकीकृत गर्न सक्छन्।
rows.bt: Shelter-related stakeholders can integrate MHPSS into programme design and implementation through the following measures.
rows.note: Proposed missing recurring terms: shelter = [Nepali wording recorded in terminology evidence]; programming = [Nepali wording recorded in terminology evidence] [Nepali wording recorded in terminology evidence] [Nepali wording recorded in terminology evidence] [Nepali wording recorded in terminology evidence].

rows.en: ▶ Including MHPSS and cultural considerations in shelter assessments (see MSP activity 1.2).
rows.ne: ▶ आश्रयसम्बन्धी लेखाजोखामा MHPSS र सांस्कृतिक पक्षहरू समावेश गर्ने (MSP गतिविधि 1.2 हेर्नुहोस्)।
rows.bt: ▶ Include MHPSS and cultural aspects in shelter-related assessments (see MSP Activity 1.2).
rows.note: Proposed missing recurring term: shelter = [Nepali wording recorded in terminology evidence].

rows.en: ▶ Advocating for improved living conditions and adequate shelter. Safe, adequate shelter supports well-being and contributes to recovery from disaster and displacement. There is also a link between physical recovery/reconstruction and psychosocial recovery: community-led repair and/or (re)construction of homes contributes to people’s dignity and sense of agency in humanitarian settings (see MSP activity 3.1).
rows.ne: ▶ जीवनयापनका अवस्था सुधार्न र पर्याप्त आश्रय उपलब्ध गराउन पैरवी गर्ने। सुरक्षित र पर्याप्त आश्रयले कल्याणलाई सहयोग पुर्‍याउँछ र विपद् तथा विस्थापनबाट पुनर्बहालीमा योगदान गर्छ। भौतिक पुनर्बहाली/पुनर्निर्माण र मनोसामाजिक पुनर्बहालीबीच पनि सम्बन्ध छ: घरहरूको मर्मत र/वा (पुनः)निर्माणका लागि समुदायको नेतृत्वमा सञ्चालित कार्यले मानवीय सङ्कटसँग सम्बन्धित परिवेशमा मानिसहरूको मर्यादा र आफैँ निर्णय तथा कार्य गर्न सक्ने अनुभूतिमा योगदान गर्छ (MSP गतिविधि 3.1 हेर्नुहोस्)।
rows.bt: ▶ Advocate to improve living conditions and provide adequate shelter. Safe and adequate shelter supports well-being and contributes to recovery from disaster and displacement. There is also a relationship between physical recovery/reconstruction and psychosocial recovery: community-led work for the repair and/or (re)construction of houses contributes to people's dignity and sense of being able to make decisions and act for themselves in settings related to humanitarian crises (see MSP Activity 3.1).
rows.note: The draft preserves the link between physical and psychosocial recovery and renders agency as a sense of being able to decide and act. The original Nepali narrows 'humanitarian settings' to settings where humanitarian assistance is provided, adding an assistance-provision condition absent from the source. The repair removes that condition.

rows.en: ▶ Providing assistance in ways that support mental health and psychosocial well-being (see MSP activity 3.1) by:

rows.en: Key consideration 10: Integrating MHPSS into water, sanitation and hygiene programming
rows.ne: मुख्य विचारणीय पक्ष 10: खानेपानी, सरसफाइ तथा स्वच्छतासम्बन्धी कार्यक्रम तर्जुमा तथा सञ्चालनमा MHPSS एकीकृत गर्ने
rows.bt: Key consideration 10: Integrating MHPSS into the design and implementation of drinking water, sanitation and hygiene programmes
rows.note: Proposed missing recurring term: programming = [Nepali wording recorded in terminology evidence] [Nepali wording recorded in terminology evidence] [Nepali wording recorded in terminology evidence] [Nepali wording recorded in terminology evidence].

rows.en: The way in which water, sanitation and hygiene is provided to affected populations can have a substantial impact on their dignity, mental health, and psychosocial well-being. Emergency-affected populations are likely to face substantially increased stress, protection risks, and illness where WASH facilities are unclean, unsafe, or culturally inappropriate; where there is a lack of menstrual hygiene management, where the water supply is inadequate; or where waste management is poor. There is also growing evidence that mental health and psychosocial well-being (e.g. levels of anxiety, self-efficacy, social connectedness) shape the extent to which people engage in certain health and hygiene behaviours during public health emergencies (e.g. handwashing, physical distancing, restricting movement). MHPSS and WASH outcomes are therefore closely interlinked.
rows.ne: प्रभावित जनसमूहलाई खानेपानी, सरसफाइ तथा स्वच्छता उपलब्ध गराउने तरिकाले उनीहरूको गरिमा, मानसिक स्वास्थ्य र मनोसामाजिक कल्याणमा उल्लेख्य प्रभाव पार्न सक्छ। खानेपानी, सरसफाइ तथा स्वच्छता (WASH) का सुविधाहरू फोहोर, असुरक्षित वा सांस्कृतिक रूपमा अनुपयुक्त भएका अवस्थामा; महिनावारी स्वच्छता व्यवस्थापनको अभाव भएका अवस्थामा; पानीको आपूर्ति अपर्याप्त भएका अवस्थामा; वा फोहोरमैला व्यवस्थापन कमजोर भएका अवस्थामा आपत्कालीन अवस्थाबाट प्रभावित जनसमूहले उल्लेख्य रूपमा बढेको तनाव, संरक्षणसम्बन्धी जोखिम र रोगको सामना गर्नुपर्ने सम्भावना हुन्छ। मानसिक स्वास्थ्य र मनोसामाजिक कल्याणले (जस्तै, चिन्ताको स्तर, आफ्नो क्षमतामाथिको विश्वास, सामाजिक आबद्धता) सार्वजनिक स्वास्थ्यसम्बन्धी आपत्कालीन अवस्थामा मानिसहरूले स्वास्थ्य र सरसफाइसम्बन्धी केही व्यवहारहरू (जस्तै, हात धुने, भौतिक दूरी कायम गर्ने, आवागमन सीमित गर्ने) कुन हदसम्म अपनाउँछन् भन्ने कुरामा प्रभाव पार्छन् भन्ने प्रमाण पनि बढ्दै गएको छ। त्यसैले MHPSS र WASH का परिणाम एकअर्कासँग घनिष्ठ रूपमा जोडिएका छन्।
rows.bt: The way drinking water, sanitation and hygiene are made available to affected populations can have a significant effect on their dignity, mental health and psychosocial well-being. In situations where drinking water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH) facilities are dirty, unsafe or culturally inappropriate; where menstrual hygiene management is lacking; where the water supply is insufficient; or where waste management is weak, populations affected by emergencies are likely to face significantly increased stress, protection-related risks and disease. There is also growing evidence that mental health and psychosocial well-being (for example, levels of anxiety, belief in one's own abilities, social connectedness) affect the extent to which people adopt certain health and sanitation-related behaviours (for example, washing hands, maintaining physical distance, limiting movement) during public health emergencies. Therefore, MHPSS and WASH outcomes are closely linked to each other.
rows.note: Stress, anxiety, self-efficacy and social connectedness are drafted without supplied matching glossary entries; none is presented as a named diagnosis. bt-divergence: The frozen forms खानेपानी, सरसफाइ तथा स्वच्छता and खानेपानी, सरसफाइ तथा स्वच्छता (WASH) specify drinking water, whereas the source says water without that restriction. The frozen forms are retained; no other substantive difference identified.

rows.en: • Promoting safety, dignity and protection in all water and sanitation activities, including BabyWASH interventions (interventions that integrate WASH across programme areas such as ECD, Nutrition, and Maternal, Newborn and Child Health to improve child health outcomes).

rows.bt: • Promote safety, dignity and protection in all water and sanitation activities, including BabyWASH interventions (BabyWASH interventions integrate water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH) into programme areas such as ECD, nutrition and maternal, newborn and child health to improve child health outcomes).

rows.bt: ▶ Meet water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH) needs as part of MHPSS activities (for example, include handwashing/hygiene in activities for children, meet the WASH needs of persons in psychiatric hospitals and institutions; see MSP Activity 3.14).

rows.en: Key consideration 11: Integrating MHPSS into food security and livelihoods programming
rows.ne: मुख्य विचारणीय पक्ष 11: खाद्य सुरक्षा तथा जीविकोपार्जनसम्बन्धी कार्यक्रम तर्जुमा तथा सञ्चालनमा MHPSS एकीकृत गर्ने
rows.bt: Key consideration 11: Integrating MHPSS into the formulation and operation of food security and livelihoods programmes
rows.note: Translated as a nonclinical programme-integration heading.

rows.en: Emergencies often disrupt access to food and cash, with many people losing their livelihoods and means of survival. This can cause severe stress and force people to engage in risky coping strategies, which may further impact their health, well-being, safety, and social relationships. For example, people may engage in risky migration or trafficking, sex work, child labour, or child marriage. The consequences of food insecurity are often gendered, with women and girls eating last and least. Harmful practices such as these can be extremely detrimental to mental health and psychosocial well-being and may have long-term effects on individual and community-wide recovery. Where food insecurity leads to malnutrition, children are at severe risk of disrupted cognitive, emotional, and social development (see key consideration 24 and MSP activity 3.5).
rows.ne: आपत्कालीन अवस्थामा प्रायः खाद्यान्न र नगदमा पहुँच अवरुद्ध हुन्छ, र धेरै मानिसहरूले आफ्नो जीविकोपार्जन तथा बाँच्ने आधार गुमाउँछन्। यसले तीव्र तनाव उत्पन्न गर्न सक्छ र मानिसहरूलाई कठिनाइको सामना गर्ने रणनीतिहरूअन्तर्गत जोखिमपूर्ण उपाय अपनाउन बाध्य पार्न सक्छ, जसले उनीहरूको स्वास्थ्य, कल्याण, सुरक्षा र सामाजिक सम्बन्धमा थप प्रभाव पार्न सक्छ। उदाहरणका लागि, मानिसहरू जोखिमपूर्ण बसाइँसराइ वा मानव बेचबिखन, यौन कार्य, बालश्रम वा बालविवाहमा संलग्न हुन सक्छन्। खाद्य असुरक्षाका परिणाम प्रायः लैङ्गिक आधारमा फरक हुन्छन्, जसमा महिला र बालिकाहरूले सबैभन्दा पछि र सबैभन्दा कम खाने गर्छन्। यस्ता हानिकारक अभ्यासहरू मानसिक स्वास्थ्य र मनोसामाजिक कल्याणका लागि अत्यन्त हानिकारक हुन सक्छन् र व्यक्ति तथा समग्र समुदायको पुनःस्थापनामा दीर्घकालीन प्रभाव पार्न सक्छन्। खाद्य असुरक्षाका कारण कुपोषण हुने अवस्थामा बालबालिकाको संज्ञानात्मक, भावनात्मक र सामाजिक विकासमा अवरोध आउने गम्भीर जोखिम हुन्छ (मुख्य विचारणीय पक्ष 24 र MSP गतिविधि 3.5 हेर्नुहोस्)।
rows.bt: In emergencies, access to food and cash is often disrupted, and many people lose their livelihoods and basis for survival. This can generate intense stress and force people to adopt risky measures as strategies for coping with difficulties, which can further affect their health, well-being, safety and social relationships. For example, people may become involved in risky migration or human trafficking, sex work, child labour or child marriage. The consequences of food insecurity often differ on the basis of gender, with women and girls eating last and least. Such harmful practices can be extremely harmful to mental health and psychosocial well-being and can have long-term effects on the recovery of individuals and the community as a whole. When food insecurity causes malnutrition, there is a serious risk of disruption to children's cognitive, emotional and social development (see Key Consideration 24 and MSP Activity 3.5).
rows.note: Severe stress and malnutrition have no supplied matching glossary entries; the source's phrase about engaging in trafficking does not specify whether people participate in it or are subjected to it, and the draft does not resolve that ambiguity.

rows.en: As community members recover from a humanitarian crisis, FSL programming can help restore their independence, sense of social identity, and meaningful participation in community life. Engaging in safe, dignified FSL activities can promote a sense of resilience, agency, and self-efficacy - factors that can be central to mental health and psychosocial well-being. MHPSS activities can help people to build skills in positive coping, communication, conflict resolution, and many other areas that facilitate effective participation in livelihoods.
rows.ne: समुदायका सदस्यहरू मानवीय सङ्कटबाट पुनः सम्हालिँदै जाँदा खाद्य सुरक्षा तथा जीविकोपार्जन (FSL) सम्बन्धी कार्यक्रमले उनीहरूको स्वावलम्बन, सामाजिक पहिचानको अनुभूति र सामुदायिक जीवनमा अर्थपूर्ण सहभागिता पुनःस्थापित गर्न मद्दत गर्न सक्छ। सुरक्षित तथा मर्यादित FSL गतिविधिमा संलग्न हुँदा कठिनाइबाट पुनः सम्हालिन सक्ने, आफ्ना निर्णयअनुसार कार्य गर्न सक्ने र आफ्नै क्षमतामा विश्वास गर्न सक्ने अनुभूति प्रवर्द्धन हुन सक्छ; यी पक्ष मानसिक स्वास्थ्य तथा मनोसामाजिक कल्याणका लागि केन्द्रीय हुन सक्छन्। MHPSS गतिविधिहरूले मानिसहरूलाई सकारात्मक रूपमा कठिनाइ सामना गर्ने, सञ्चार गर्ने, द्वन्द्व समाधान गर्ने तथा जीविकोपार्जनमा प्रभावकारी सहभागिता सहज बनाउने अन्य धेरै क्षेत्रका सीप विकास गर्न मद्दत गर्न सक्छन्।
rows.bt: As community members recover from a humanitarian crisis, food security and livelihoods (FSL) programmes can help restore their self-reliance, sense of social identity and meaningful participation in community life. Engagement in safe and dignified FSL activities can promote a sense of being able to recover from difficulties, act according to one's own decisions and believe in one's own abilities; these aspects can be central to mental health and psychosocial well-being. MHPSS activities can help people develop skills in coping positively with difficulties, communicating, resolving conflict and many other areas that facilitate effective participation in livelihoods.
rows.note: Nonclinical programme benefits and skills are drafted in ordinary descriptive language. Mental health and psychosocial well-being reuse supplied unreviewed candidates. Propose glossary entries for resilience, agency, self-efficacy and positive coping, preserving respectively recovery from adversity, capacity to decide and act, belief in one's capabilities, and constructive ways of handling difficulties.

rows.en: FSL actors can integrate MHPSS into programming by:
rows.ne: खाद्य सुरक्षा तथा जीविकोपार्जन (FSL) का सम्बद्ध पक्षहरूले निम्न तरिकाले कार्यक्रम तर्जुमा तथा सञ्चालनमा MHPSS एकीकृत गर्न सक्छन्।
rows.bt: Stakeholders in food security and livelihoods (FSL) can integrate MHPSS into programme formulation and operation in the following ways.

rows.en: ▶ Including MHPSS-related factors in needs assessments: e.g. assessing social and cultural factors related to food security, nutrition and food aid such as dietary beliefs and practices, household roles, and cultural taboos (see MSP activity 1.1). Assessments should also consider the extent to which people recovering from mental health conditions can access livelihoods (see MSP activity 1.2 and Sphere Livelihoods standard 7.2).
rows.ne: ▶ आवश्यकताको लेखाजोखामा MHPSS सम्बन्धी पक्षहरू समावेश गर्ने: उदाहरणका लागि, खानपानसम्बन्धी विश्वास र अभ्यास, घरपरिवारभित्रका भूमिका र सांस्कृतिक वर्जनाजस्ता खाद्य सुरक्षा, पोषण र खाद्य सहायतासँग सम्बन्धित सामाजिक तथा सांस्कृतिक पक्षहरूको लेखाजोखा गर्ने (MSP गतिविधि 1.1 हेर्नुहोस्)। लेखाजोखामा मानसिक स्वास्थ्यसम्बन्धी अवस्थाहरूबाट निको हुँदै गरेका मानिसहरूले जीविकोपार्जनमा कुन हदसम्म पहुँच पाउन सक्छन् भन्ने कुरा पनि विचार गर्नुपर्छ (MSP गतिविधि 1.2 र Sphere को जीविकोपार्जन मानक 7.2 हेर्नुहोस्)।
rows.bt: ▶ Include MHPSS-related aspects in needs assessments: for example, assess social and cultural aspects related to food security, nutrition and food assistance, such as beliefs and practices concerning eating, roles within households and cultural taboos (see MSP Activity 1.1). Assessments should also consider the extent to which people recovering from mental health conditions can access livelihoods (see MSP Activity 1.2 and Sphere Livelihoods Standard 7.2).
rows.note: The supplied plural condition term is used without adding a daily-functioning impairment requirement, and recovery remains an ongoing process.

rows.en: ▶ Providing assistance in ways that support mental health and psychosocial well-being (see MSP activity 3.1) by:
rows.ne: ▶ मानसिक स्वास्थ्य तथा मनोसामाजिक कल्याणमा सहयोग पुग्ने गरी निम्न तरिकाले सहायता प्रदान गर्ने (MSP गतिविधि 3.1 हेर्नुहोस्)।
rows.bt: ▶ Provide assistance in the following ways so as to support mental health and psychosocial well-being (see MSP Activity 3.1).
rows.note: Mental health and psychosocial well-being wording reuses the supplied unreviewed candidates.

rows.en: • Promoting the participation of target communities in FSL programming and long-term food-security planning, including groups at heightened risk such as women, persons with disabilities, persons with mental health conditions and older adults. Engaging community members in recovery efforts not only improves the appropriateness and effectiveness of interventions but can also foster a sense of agency and combat feelings of helplessness and resignation (see Sphere Food security standard 5).
rows.ne: • महिला, अपाङ्गता भएका व्यक्तिहरू, मानसिक स्वास्थ्यसम्बन्धी अवस्थाहरू भएका व्यक्तिहरू र ज्येष्ठ वयस्कहरूजस्ता बढी जोखिममा रहेका समूहहरूलाई समेत समेटेर लक्षित समुदायहरूको FSL कार्यक्रम तर्जुमा तथा कार्यान्वयनमा र खाद्य सुरक्षाको दीर्घकालीन योजना निर्माणमा सहभागिता प्रवर्द्धन गर्ने। पुनःस्थापनाका प्रयासहरूमा समुदायका सदस्यहरूलाई संलग्न गराउँदा हस्तक्षेपहरूको उपयुक्तता र प्रभावकारिता बढ्छ। यसले आफ्नो निर्णय र कार्यमार्फत प्रभाव पार्न सक्ने अनुभूति पनि विकास गर्न सक्छ र असहायता तथा हार मानेको भावनालाई कम गर्न सक्छ (Sphere को खाद्य सुरक्षा मानक 5 हेर्नुहोस्)।
rows.bt: • Promote the participation of targeted communities in the formulation and implementation of FSL programmes and in the development of long-term plans for food security, including groups at greater risk such as women, persons with disabilities, persons with mental health-related conditions and older adults. Involving community members in rehabilitation efforts increases the appropriateness and effectiveness of interventions. This can also develop a sense of being able to have an effect through one's own decisions and actions and can reduce feelings of helplessness and giving up (see Sphere food security standard 5).
rows.note: People with mental health conditions remain a broad population category without an added impairment criterion; the possible benefits for agency and feelings of helplessness or resignation remain qualified as possibilities. The BT makes improved appropriateness and effectiveness merely possible. The source asserts that engagement improves both, while qualifying the benefits for agency, helplessness and resignation as possibilities. The repair makes that distinction explicit.
